notes: flaky-test-qa was not rerun: its QA-3 pass at 6972530 covers the tests, and the 6972530..5c85c6b test change is one caller test's expected text, verified by rust-qa. Acceptance evidence is in acceptance-5c85c6b.log. Prior rounds' dispositions: R5-QA1-RSH-001 (duplicate of the documented judge bound) and R5-QA1-RQA-QA-001 (pre-existing pyo3 link issue, not run in CI).

deliverable_checks.item: Acceptance commands, just lint and just test at 5c85c6b (REQ-QA-001)
deliverable_checks.notes: Every entry shows test result ok and rc=0 on rustc 1.94.1 at HEAD 5c85c6b. The worktree HEAD ref is sprint/r-5-jev-wire-envelope. I could not resolve the ref to a sha because I have no shell, so the sha match rests on the log header.
`let Pairs(pairs) = Pairs::<K, V>::deserialize(deserializer)?;` is present. It sits at line 194, not 193 as the notes said.

deliverable_checks.item: New test in the NFR-SAG-0002 acceptance row (REQ-QA-003)
deliverable_checks.notes: test_malformed_body_hint_is_fix_the_body is in the row. The log shows it ran with 1 passed.

deliverable_checks.item: ADR-SAG-0029 list entry in the sprint adrs list
deliverable_checks.notes: The (c) disposition 'serde_json encode / decode failure' maps to INPUT_INVALID with category and line/column only. The entry matches that text.
The amendment keeps all HTTP in sc-jev and puts the pure mapping in jev::v1. It matches the sprint text. No '(Proposed, r-5)' marker remains in docs/architecture.md.
Parse failures give INPUT_INVALID with the serde category, position and a 'fix the <what>' hint, and carry no body bytes. This follows ADR-SAG-0029 (c) and ADR-SAG-0020.
It covers three failure kinds: eof, data and syntax. It asserts the code is INPUT_INVALID, the hint contains 'fix the', and the hint holds no secret text, 'encoded' or 'bug'.

fenced_json.gate_reason: The 6972530..5c85c6b delta has no findings. REQ-QA-001, REQ-QA-002 and REQ-QA-003 are closed. The execution log shows every named command, just lint and just test passing at 5c85c6b. The ADR-0029 list entry, the ADR-SAG-0012 amendment, the decode_failed routing and the changed test are consistent with the sprint doc and docs/architecture.md.

fenced_json.notes: I could not run git commands, so I confirmed the worktree branch from .git/worktrees/r-5-jev-wire-envelope/HEAD, which points at refs/heads/sprint/r-5-jev-wire-envelope. I did not resolve that ref to commit 5c85c6b. I read the files in the worktree as they are. ARCH-010 is closed: ADR-SAG-0029 is in the sprint doc adrs list at line 54. ARCH-011 and ARCH-012 are closed: the Active ADR-SAG-0012 r-5 subsection (docs/architecture.md:1035-1041) now names the pure CheckResponse::into_answers mapping in sc_decision_schema::jev::v1, with no HTTP or I/O, and keeps every Jev HTTP operation in sc-jev. The ADR-SAG-0030 index and header text match this. The code at jev/v1.rs:760 and the sprint sample at line 297 agree with the amended ADR. ARCH-013 is closed: Question::from_json (payload.rs:244) and PayloadBundle::decode (payload.rs:427 and 519) route through decode_failed (payload.rs:104). That helper returns INPUT_INVALID with only the serde category and line/column, which is the ADR-SAG-0029 (c) disposition. Two decode sites in sc-decision-schema do not use decode_failed (jev/v1.rs:602 and :722, and variants.rs:100 and llm/v1.rs:35 map errors themselves). I judged these as outside the ARCH-013 delta, and the ADR-SAG-0029 (c) row covers general serde failures. They are not raised as findings, but you may want a quick look. I found no std::sync::Mutex guards held across .await in the reviewed targets.
